newsitem.title: UK: UK leading shares close at new record peak.
newsitem.headline: UK leading shares close at new record peak.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index of leading UK shares pushed further into uncharted territory, closing at new record on Monday, spurred by a strong lead from Wall Street and renewed takeover speculation, dealers said.
The benchmark index settled 24.7 points higher at 4,115.7. At 1642 GMT, SEAQ volume registered only 382.0 million shares.
"Volume has been thin, but the market has quite a good feel to it," said one dealer.
He was expecting strong earnings growth to carry UK blue chips, up about 11 percent this year, higher still in 1997.
The only wild card, he said, will be Wall Street, where shares have climbed by roughly 29 percent this year.
"But worries about a correction on Wall Street are always looming," he added.
The Dow also was trading at record levels, up about 22 points, when London markets closed.
Today's rally was broad based, with FTSE 100 advancers outpacing decliners by a margin of about four to one.
